name: Four Star Foods
old_description: Supplying & Distributing Quality Poultry, Pork, Beef, Seafood, & other Proteins to Retailers, Restaurants, & Food Service Establishments throughout
about:
Four Star Foods, Inc. operates from Chicago, Illinois, where it recently relocated to a facility near the International Produce Market after decades in the historic Fulton Meat Market. The business is family-owned, with four generations of experience in meat wholesaling in Chicago, though the exact founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company functions as both a wholesale distributor and a USDA-inspected processor (establishment P18395/M2514), supplying poultry, pork, beef, seafood, and other proteins. It offers specialty cutting services, runs a temperature-controlled truck fleet with CDL-licensed drivers for five-day-a-week delivery, and provides freezer rental. Specific facility square footage, employee count, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Four Star Foods serves grocery stores, retail outlets, restaurants, and food-service establishments across Chicago, Milwaukee, and Northwest Indiana. Its vendor partnerships include Midwestern farmers, though specific brand names are not listed.

The company emphasizes supply-chain value and long-term customer relationships, rooted in its multi-generational family heritage in the Chicago meat trade. Its USDA partnership ensures that both facility and products meet rigorous federal standards, and it highlights an employee-focused culture with competitive compensation, retirement, and health benefits.

name: Four Star Wire & Cable, Manufacturers of the MyStarSound Pro Audio, Video, Stage, Lighting and Connectivity products
Fourbital Factory
old_description: Whether you're ordering branded merchandise, launching a retail collection, or testing a new product idea, Fourbital Factory offers flexible manufacturing programs designed around your goals.
about:
Fourbital Factory operates from Burlington, Vermont, where it designs and produces custom beanies entirely in-house. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but it presents itself as a Vermont-based manufacturer focused on domestic production.

The factory specializes in custom knit beanies, offering private-label, small-batch, and scaled production programs. Capabilities include 1×1 and 3×1 rib, chunky rib, and custom jacquard knitting in acrylic or merino wool, with over 40 acrylic and 15 wool color options. Finishing services cover embroidered patches, woven labels, pom-poms, and custom packaging. The vertically integrated workflow moves from design through prototyping (about one week) to full production (three to five weeks) and shipping (three to seven business days), with minimums as low as 25 units.

Fourbital serves a broad range of clients, including apparel and outdoor brands, retail collections, subscription boxes, ski resorts, breweries, universities, nonprofits, hospitality groups, sports teams, and corporate merchandise programs. A noted case study highlights a partnership with Darn Tough, transforming leftover sock yarn into wool beanies. The company also supports emerging brands, Kickstarter campaigns, and seasonal collaborations through its low-minimum model.

The company emphasizes quality, flexibility, and true partnership, positioning its domestic, small-batch approach as an alternative to overseas production. By keeping manufacturing local, Fourbital aims to move quickly, communicate clearly, and deliver craftsmanship that sets clients’ products apart, while supporting local jobs and offering “100% tariff-proof” production.

name: Fox Valley Metal Fab, Inc.
old_description: Fox Valley Metal Fabrication offers full-service welding, machining and fabrication.
about:
Fox Valley Metal Fab, Inc. operates in Appleton, Wisconsin. The business began as Hietpas Welding, Inc., founded by Bruce Hietpas. On December 6, 2019, Clint La Rue acquired the company from Hietpas, who continues to contribute expertise and estimating support. The firm now trades under the Fox Valley Metal Fab name.

The shop delivers full-service welding, machining, and fabrication. Welding capabilities span TIG, MIG, stick, and gas processes, performed by certified welders on all metal types. Machining includes milling and lathe work. Fabrication services cover shearing, forming, rolling, punching, plasma cutting, and pipe bending. Structural fabrication produces stairs, platforms, canopies, and handrails. The company also provides mobile, on-site welding and repair. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

The company serves customers needing custom metal fabrication and welding, including structural and decorative projects. While specific industries are not listed, the service range suggests clients in construction, industrial maintenance, and custom metalwork. Jobs of any size are accepted.

Fox Valley Metal Fab emphasizes a customer-first philosophy, aiming to provide courteous, professional service. It cites continuous equipment upgrades to remain competitive and notes that its certified welders enable it to handle projects of any scale.

name: Fpb Cable
old_description: FPB's Preferred Cable offers exciting sports networks like ESPN U, NFL NETWORK and BIG TEN NETWORK.
about:
Frankfort Plant Board (FPB) operates as a municipal utility in Frankfort, Kentucky, providing electric, water, and cable‑telecom services to the community. Governed as a public board, it serves the capital city and surrounding areas with locally controlled infrastructure.

The cable division markets tiered television packages—Limited, Classic, and Preferred—along with à la carte premium channels (HBO, Showtime, Starz, Cinemax) and a Sports Plus add‑on. It supplies set‑top boxes (standard definition, high definition, and HD‑DVR), digital cable cards, and a TV Everywhere streaming platform accessible on mobile devices. The board also manages electric and water distribution, and has recently added a community solar project and energy‑efficiency programs.

Residential and small‑business customers in the Frankfort service area make up the core subscriber base. The utility also supports local government and educational access channels, including Cable 10 community programming and Kentucky Educational Television feeds.

FPB emphasizes local customer service, bundled utility billing, and community ownership as differentiators. The board notes that its integrated electric, water, and telecom operations allow coordinated infrastructure investment and a single point of contact for residents.

name: Frank's Custom Furniture
old_description: Our mission at Frank’s Custom Furniture is to provide our customers with furniture of the highest quality and craftsmanship, whatever your budget, that lasts for generations.
about:
Frank's Custom Furniture operates from Foreston, Minnesota, where it was founded in 1991 by Mike and Tamra Frank. The couple began with a modest lineup of made-to-order pieces, re-glue repairs, and antique restoration, and have since expanded into a full-time shop serving the region for over three decades.

The company produces solid-wood furniture and cabinetry using traditional joinery such as dovetailing, lathe-turned veneer work, and handwoven caning—a craft they describe as a lost art. Services span custom design, cabinet building and refacing, refinishing, refurbishing, hand stripping, touch-ups, and commercial millwork, along with insurance-claim restoration. All pieces are built from Minnesota-grown timber in a facility that emphasizes handcrafted methods over automated production.

Customers include homeowners seeking heirloom-quality dining sets, bedroom suites, and built-ins; businesses needing commercial casework and trim; and insurance adjusters requiring restoration after damage. The shop also supplies unfinished furniture and replicates antique styles from Mission to Rustic.

The Franks attribute their reputation to attention to detail, durability, and a collaborative design process that treats each project as a partnership. Their use of locally sourced, eco-friendly lumber and preservation of hand-caned seating distinguish them in a market dominated by mass-produced alternatives.

name: Franklin Farms
old_description: We are equal parts wisdom and energy. With inspirations both classic and modern. We help you achieve balance as well as fun. Here's to your good health and great taste.
about:
Franklin Farms traces its roots to 1981, when it started on a mushroom farm in Franklin, Connecticut. The company is now headquartered in Boulder, Colorado. No founders are named in the source material, and ownership structure is not disclosed.

The company manufactures a wide range of plant-based proteins, including veggie burgers, breakfast items, veggie balls, seitan, tofu (organic super firm, organic, ready-bake kits), plant-powered meat, seasoned seitan, edamame, tempeh, fusion tofu, chickpea tofu and tempeh, and plant-based tuna. Production processes involve mixing, splicing, mingling, and dicing flavor-forward, high-quality plant proteins, with an explicit commitment to avoiding genetic engineering. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

Franklin Farms serves retail grocery and foodservice channels, targeting consumers seeking meatless meals that span day parts and taste profiles. Its products appear in natural and conventional grocery aisles, though specific customer names are not provided. The company positions itself in the plant-based food manufacturing, vegetarian and vegan foods, and retail food product sectors.

Its stated differentiation rests on non-GMO ingredient sourcing, flavor-forward formulations, and a product portfolio designed for both quick bites and sit-down dinners.

name: Franks Manufacturing
old_description: Franks Mfg. Co. specializes in heavy gauge, high volume thermoforming and custom plastic products. All members of the team are dedicated to providing quality custom plastic and vacuum formed parts.
about:
Franks Manufacturing operates from San Antonio, Texas, where the plant opened in 1980 as a family-owned venture producing Texas Best Lick Feeders for the agricultural liquid feed industry. The company remains family-owned and operated; ownership passed from father to son in November 2006, and James Franks serves as president.

The company specializes in heavy-gauge, high-volume thermoforming and vacuum forming of custom plastic products. Its capabilities include CNC routing on 3-axis machines handling sheets up to 60 by 120 inches, mold production, prototyping, and design services using MasterCAM and SolidWorks. Materials range from polyethylene and acrylics to non-ferrous metals such as aluminum, brass, and copper, as well as composites, foam, and wood-based boards. Franks describes itself as one of the largest custom vacuum formers in South Texas, serving both small and large volume orders.

Customers span agriculture, oil and gas, medical, grocery, construction, waste management, automotive, and government infrastructure. Concrete product lines include Protein Lick Feeders for agriculture, open-top containment tanks used in the Eagle Ford, Permian Basin, and Bakken shale fields, store bins for grocery retailers, and cough/sneeze shields for medical facilities. The client roster includes Fortune 500 companies.

Franks emphasizes a culture of teamwork, loyalty, respect, and integrity, aiming to deliver outstanding products with dedicated customer service. It holds SBA small business certification, veteran-owned status, and SCTRA, ESBE, SBE, and VBE certifications, and is a member of the San Antonio Manufacturers Association.

name: Freedom Electronics LLC / Esco
old_description: for reduced inventory, higher quality, and profitability for distributors, technicians, and station owners in the retail petroleum industry.
about:
Founded in 1998, Freedom Electronics operates from a 41,000-square-foot headquarters in Kennesaw, Georgia, with additional branches in Florida and Michigan. The company employs over 100 professionals, including engineers, certified technicians, and warehouse personnel, across its three locations.

The firm designs and manufactures engineered drop-in replacement parts for fuel dispensers and point-of-sale systems, including printers, displays, keyboards, and control boards. It also runs a remanufacturing program that applies advanced coatings and AI-enhanced inspection to extend component life, and manages a core-exchange system that credits customers for returned units.

Freedom Electronics serves distributors, technicians, and station owners in the retail petroleum industry. Its product line covers major dispenser brands such as Gilbarco, Wayne, VeriFone, Tokheim, Bennett, and Gasboy, providing both new aftermarket components and remanufactured assemblies.

The company emphasizes engineering innovations—advanced coatings, improved inspection technologies, and artificial intelligence integration—to produce more durable remanufactured parts that lower maintenance costs for retailers. A core-charge refund policy and dedicated technical support round out its service offering.
